tier_reason: The README table matches a first-party criterion benchmark in benches/rasterize_bench.rs (TiTanF, Fontdue, RustType, ab_glyph on the same font, string and sizes), but no CPU model, rustc version or RUSTFLAGS are stated and the bench font is not in the repo, so it falls short of A.

corrections.language: Rust (no_std with alloc, zero dependencies; SSE2/AVX2/NEON SIMD paths)
corrections.workload: Rasterizing every character of one 106-character string (30 CJK ideographs plus A-Z, a-z, 0-9 and 14 ASCII punctuation marks; the README says 84 characters, but the MESSAGE constant in benches/rasterize_bench.rs has 106, derived from page data) with NotoSansSC-Medium.ttf at 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 200 and 320 px into owned coverage bitmaps, glyph cache off (get_char::<false>), criterion medians with 4 s measurement time per case.
corrections.claimed_speedup: README criterion medians, TiTanF / Fontdue / RustType / ab_glyph: 10px 71.0 us / 54.3 / 245.6 / 222.6; 20px 123.2 us / 83.7 / 224.2 / 279.4; 40px 237.3 us / 178.2 / 356.2 / 485.0; 80px 495.4 us / 401.7 / 966.4 / 821.1; 160px 1.08 ms / 1.02 / 2.29 / 2.16; 200px 1.45 ms / 1.60 / 3.21 / 3.07; 320px 3.13 ms / 4.02 / 7.27 / 6.77. TiTanF is 1.5x-3.5x faster than RustType and 1.7x-3.1x faster than ab_glyph across sizes (derived from page data); Fontdue is faster than TiTanF from 10px through 160px, and TiTanF leads it only at 200px (1.1x) and 320px (1.3x) (derived from page data).
corrections.baseline: RustType and ab_glyph (long-standing, widely used pure-Rust glyph rasterizers); Fontdue, another pure-Rust rasterizer, also measured and faster at 10-160px; FreeType and HarfBuzz are not measured
corrections.compiler_and_flags: cargo bench with the default bench profile (release, opt-level 3); Cargo.toml has no [profile] section and no RUSTFLAGS or target-cpu setting is given, so the rustc version and the SIMD level actually compiled in are unstated
corrections.stars_or_usage: 3 stars, 0 forks; crates.io titanf 3.0.0 with 2,559 total downloads (199 recent) as of 2026-10-03
corrections.caveats: First-party criterion benchmark (benches/rasterize_bench.rs, adapted from Fontdue's bench) with no CPU model, rustc version or run conditions stated, and one font and one string. load_font eagerly converts every glyph of the font into raster-ready geometry outside the timed loop, while RustType and ab_glyph parse each outline inside it, so the per-call times exclude TiTanF's front-loaded parse cost (Fontdue also preprocesses at load). The bench font NotoSansSC-Medium.ttf is gitignored (*.ttf) and absent from the repo, so cargo bench does not build from a fresh clone and the font version is unstated. The README says 84 characters; the bench string has 106. Fontdue beats TiTanF from 10px to 160px. Baselines are pure-Rust rasterizers, not FreeType; no claim against FreeType or HarfBuzz exists. Tiny new project (3 stars, first crate release 2025-10-16).

notes: RustType and ab_glyph are recognisable incumbents within Rust but not the category's C/C++ incumbents, so baseline_in_list stays false; language is Rust (not in the correctable list, set in corrections for the orchestrator to apply as an override). Same glyphs, sizes and output type for all four libraries, but the work split differs (eager whole-font preprocessing at load for TiTanF).

tier_reason: The only evidence is the first-party README line '2x to 5x faster parsing than opentype.js'; the repo (src/, demo/, index.html) contains no benchmark code, corpus, machine or timing table, so it is a number without methodology.

corrections.language: JavaScript (three source files: src/Typr.js, src/Typr.U.js, src/Typr.U.SVG.js; optional HarfBuzz WASM shaping)
corrections.stars_or_usage: about 1.0k stars, 80 forks; main text engine of the Photopea image editor (README)
corrections.baseline: opentype.js (the widely used JavaScript OpenType font parser, a recognisable incumbent in JavaScript); HarfBuzz and FreeType are not measured
corrections.caveats: First-party one-line README claim with no benchmark code, font corpus, opentype.js version, JavaScript engine, machine or timing numbers anywhere in the repo (demo/ holds three fonts and two HTML pages with no timing code), so it cannot be reproduced. Parsing depth is not shown to be equivalent: Typr.parse fills glyf with null placeholders and parses each glyph lazily via _parseGlyf, and GPOS and GDEF are commented out of its table parser list, so part of the gap may be less work done at parse time. The baseline is opentype.js, not HarfBuzz or FreeType, and parse speed says nothing about shaping or rasterization. Recent commits are mostly 'Add files via upload'; last commit 2025-08-28, more than 12 months ago.

notes: opentype.js is a recognisable JavaScript incumbent but not HarfBuzz or FreeType, so baseline_in_list stays false; language JavaScript set in corrections for the orchestrator to apply as an override. maintenance_status moved from active to stale because the last commit (2025-08-28, gh-pages default branch) is over 12 months before today. One WebSearch found only copies of the README claim, no independent measurement.

tier_reason: First-party IPython %%timeit sessions in the README, with the PyICU harness code shown, but no benchmark script in the repo and no CPU, OS, Python, PyICU or ICU version stated.

corrections.language: Cython (CPython C extension with a Python API and .pxd files for cimport from Cython)
corrections.baseline: ICU's character BreakIterator called through PyICU (the Python binding to ICU's C++ library), driven by a Python generator; also pyuegc, uniseg and grapheme (the other Python grapheme splitters)
corrections.workload: Splitting one short string of 15 extended grapheme clusters ('Hello', '!', spaces, two emoji ZWJ sequences with skin-tone modifiers and the Devanagari word अनुच्छेद) into a list of grapheme strings (UAX #29), timed with IPython %%timeit (mean of 7 runs of 100,000 or 1,000,000 loops).
corrections.claimed_speedup: README %%timeit means: ugrapheme grapheme_split 337 ns vs PyICU BreakIterator loop 2.84 us (8.4x, derived from page data; README says 8x); pyuegc EGC 8.19 us vs 337 ns (24x; the section heading says 25x); uniseg 14.6 us vs 340 ns (README says 45x; 43x derived from page data; wrong split of a Devanagari conjunct); grapheme 17.4 us vs 332 ns (52x; also wrong split).
corrections.stars_or_usage: 40 stars, 2 forks; PyPI ugrapheme 0.8 with wheels for CPython 3.8+
corrections.caveats: First-party IPython %%timeit sessions on a single 15-grapheme string; no CPU, OS, Python, Cython, PyICU or ICU version stated (a separate ASCII throughput remark cites only 'a fast 2024 laptop') and no benchmark script in the repo. The PyICU harness converts the input to icu.UnicodeString, calls nextBoundary() once per grapheme through the binding inside a Python generator and builds a Python str per slice, so the 8.4x gap mostly measures CPython and binding overhead on a tiny input, not ICU's C++ segmentation; there is no comparison against ICU from C or C++ or on long text. Unicode versions are not matched: ugrapheme passes the Unicode 16.0 GraphemeBreakTest, while the ICU and pyuegc versions used are not given; uniseg and grapheme produce wrong splits, so their ratios compare unequal output. CPython-only extension, not callable from C++. Belongs in Unicode segmentation (wave 3 unicode-utf8), not font shaping. Last commit and last release (0.8) on 2024-10-28.

notes: PyICU wraps ICU, a listed incumbent for the unicode-utf8 category, so baseline_in_list is set to true with the binding-overhead caveat; suggest a category override to unicode-utf8 (category is not correctable here) and language Cython. Minor README slip: it says PyICU boundaries index a UTF-8 representation, but ICU UnicodeString offsets are UTF-16 code units; this does not affect the timings. Metadata (0BSD, 40 stars, last commit 2024-10-28, stale) confirmed.
